# docker_buildx_builder (Resource)

A BuildKit builder run by the daemon as a `docker-container` driver node, the same container and state volume `docker buildx create --driver docker-container --bootstrap` makes, created through the Engine API without the buildx CLI. The container `buildx_buildkit_<node>` runs `moby/buildkit` privileged with the state volume `buildx_buildkit_<node>_state`; readiness is checked by listing BuildKit workers over `buildctl dial-stdio` in the container. Pass `name` to `docker_image.build.builder`, or use `endpoint` with `buildctl --addr` (`tcp_address` when `tcp_port` is set). The buildx CLI's own instance list (`~/.docker/buildx/instances`) is not written, so `docker buildx ls` does not show the builder until `docker buildx create --name <name> --driver docker-container` is run, which adopts the same container. Only the `docker-container` driver creates a container; the `remote` driver only checks and reports a BuildKit daemon run elsewhere, selected in builds by its `endpoint`; the `cloud` driver checks and reports a Docker Build Cloud builder, whose access token lives only in memory for the connection. With the provider's `owner` set, the node container and state volume carry the owner label. Every argument except `keep_state` and `adopt` forces a new resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "docker_buildx_builder" "ci" {
  name            = "ci"
  buildkitd_flags = "--allow-insecure-entitlement=network.host --debug"

  buildkitd_config_content = <<-EOT
    [worker.oci]
      max-parallelism = 4
  EOT

  # Pin the platforms this node advertises first (docker buildx create --platform).
  platform = ["linux/amd64", "linux/arm64"]

  docker_container {
    image        = "moby/buildkit:buildx-stable-1"
    memory       = 4294967296 # 4 GiB
    cpu_quota    = 200000     # two CPUs per 100 ms period
    cpu_period   = 100000
    default_load = true
    env = {
      HTTPS_PROXY = "http://proxy.internal:3128"
    }
  }

  # Optional: also serve BuildKit on TCP (unauthenticated).
  tcp_port = 1234
}

output "buildkit_endpoint" {
  # e.g. buildctl --addr docker-container://buildx_buildkit_ci0 debug workers
  value = docker_buildx_builder.ci.endpoint
}

output "buildkit_tcp" {
  value = docker_buildx_builder.ci.tcp_address
}

output "buildkit_version" {
  value = docker_buildx_builder.ci.buildkit_version
}

# A BuildKit daemon run elsewhere (docker buildx create --driver remote).
# Nothing is created on the Docker daemon; builds select it by endpoint.
resource "docker_buildx_builder" "remote" {
  name     = "remote"
  driver   = "remote"
  endpoint = "tcp://buildkit.internal:1234"

  remote {
    cacert     = "${path.module}/certs/ca.pem"
    cert       = "${path.module}/certs/client-cert.pem"
    key        = "${path.module}/certs/client-key.pem"
    servername = "buildkit.internal"
  }
}

# A Docker Build Cloud builder (docker buildx create --driver cloud myorg/default).
# The provider logs in at auth.docker.io with its Docker Hub credential
# (registry_auth for docker.io, else the docker config) and reaches BuildKit at
# build-cloud.docker.com:443; the access token stays in memory, never in state.
resource "docker_buildx_builder" "cloud" {
  name     = "cloud"
  driver   = "cloud"
  endpoint = "myorg/default"
}

# Build several platforms at once on the cloud builder, e.g. in docker_image:
#
#   build {
#     context   = "${path.module}/app"
#     builder   = docker_buildx_builder.cloud.id # cloud://myorg/default
#     platforms = ["linux/amd64", "linux/arm64"]
#     outputs   = ["type=registry"] # push the image index
#   }
#
# Loading a multi-platform result into the daemon needs its containerd image store.
output "cloud_builder" {
  value = docker_buildx_builder.cloud.id
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Builder name, as for `docker buildx create --name`; pass it to `docker_image.build.builder`. Forces replacement.

### Optional

- `adopt` (Boolean) Take over an object whose `io.terraform.provider.owner` label names a different owner than the provider's `owner` argument (for example after `terraform import`). Without it, planning such an object fails. Only checked when the provider sets `owner`. Default `false`.
- `append` (Boolean) Whether this node joins an existing builder of the same `name` (`--append`). The builder must already have a node on the daemon, and `node` must differ from its nodes. With `false` (default) creating fails when the builder already exists. Destroy removes only this node. Forces replacement.
- `bootstrap` (Boolean) Whether to start the builder and wait until BuildKit lists its workers (`--bootstrap`). With `false` the container is only created. Default `true`. Forces replacement.
- `buildkitd_config` (String) Path of a local `buildkitd.toml` (`--buildkitd-config`), read at apply and copied to `/etc/buildkit/buildkitd.toml` in the container. Conflicts with `buildkitd_config_content`. Forces replacement.
- `buildkitd_config_content` (String) Content of `buildkitd.toml`, copied like `buildkitd_config`. Forces replacement.
- `buildkitd_flags` (String) Flags for buildkitd (`--buildkitd-flags`), whitespace-separated with no shell quoting, e.g. `"--debug --allow-insecure-entitlement=security.insecure"`. Default `--allow-insecure-entitlement=network.host`, like buildx. Forces replacement.
- `docker_container` (Block, Optional) Settings for the BuildKit container (`--driver-opt`). Changing anything here forces a new resource. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--docker_container))
- `driver` (String) Builder driver: `docker-container` (default), `remote` or `cloud`. `docker-container` runs BuildKit in a container on the provider's daemon; `remote` is a BuildKit daemon run elsewhere and reached at `endpoint` (TLS in the `remote` block); `cloud` is a Docker Build Cloud builder named by `endpoint` (`<org>/<builder>`), reached at build-cloud.docker.com:443 with a token from auth.docker.io obtained with the provider's Docker Hub credential (`registry_auth` for docker.io, else the docker config). `docker` is the daemon's built-in builder (use `docker_image` without `build.builder`); `kubernetes` is not supported (it needs the Kubernetes API). Forces replacement.
- `endpoint` (String) BuildKit address of the builder, for `buildctl --addr` and `docker_image.build.builder`. With `driver = "remote"` it is required: the remote BuildKit's `tcp://host:port` or `unix:///path` (the `docker buildx create --driver remote` endpoint argument). With `driver = "cloud"` it is required: the Docker Build Cloud builder as `<org>/<builder>` (`cloud://<org>/<builder>` is also accepted), the `docker buildx create --driver cloud` endpoint argument; `id` is then `cloud://<org>/<builder>`, which `docker_image.build.builder` and `docker_buildx_bake.builder` accept. With `docker-container` it is computed: `docker-container://buildx_buildkit_<node>`. Forces replacement.
- `keep_state` (Boolean) Whether to keep the state volume (build cache) on destroy (`docker buildx rm --keep-state`). Default `false`. Updated in place.
- `node` (String) Node name (`--node`); the node container is `buildx_buildkit_<node>`. Default `<name>0`, like buildx. Forces replacement.
- `platform` (List of String) Platforms this node is pinned to (`--platform`), listed first in `platforms`. buildx keeps pins in its client-side store; the provider stores them as a label on the node container. Forces replacement.
- `remote` (Block, Optional) TLS settings of a `remote` driver builder (`--driver-opt cacert=,cert=,key=,servername=`). Only with `driver = "remote"`. Changing anything here forces a new resource. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--remote))
- `tcp_port` (Number) Host port on which BuildKit is also served over TCP: buildkitd listens on `tcp://0.0.0.0:1234` in the container and the port is published on this host port. Unauthenticated and unencrypted; bind it only on trusted networks. Forces replacement.

### Read-Only

- `builder` (Attributes) The builder object field by field (name, driver, last activity, nodes with endpoint, status, BuildKit version, platforms, labels, GC policy). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--builder))
- `buildkit_version` (String) BuildKit daemon version of the first node (identity, not one of the six version names; see naming_questions).
- `buildx_version` (String) The buildx release whose output format and semantics this type mirrors (pin v0.38.2); not a runtime binary, the provider never runs buildx.
- `container_name` (String) Name of the node container, `buildx_buildkit_<node>`.
- `content_sha256` (String) SHA-256 of inspect_json, to detect drift without diffing the document.
- `docker_server_version` (String) Docker Engine version of the daemon (GET /version Version).
- `engine_api_version` (String) Engine API version negotiated with the daemon for this read/apply.
- `id` (String) ID of the BuildKit node container.
- `inspect_json` (String, Sensitive) The builder and its nodes as one JSON document (the `docker buildx inspect` view, keys as in `buildx ls --format json` Builder object). Sensitive: driver options carry env.* values.
- `labels` (Map of String) BuildKit worker labels of the node (`org.mobyproject.buildkit.worker.*`). Empty when `bootstrap` is false.
- `platforms` (List of String) Platforms the builder can build for: the `platform` pins, then what the BuildKit workers report, e.g. `["linux/amd64", "linux/386"]`. Only the pins when `bootstrap` is false.
- `tcp_address` (String) TCP address of BuildKit, `tcp://<daemon host>:<tcp_port>`, when `tcp_port` is set: the host of the provider's `tcp://`/`ssh://` daemon address, else `127.0.0.1`. Null without `tcp_port`.
- `volume_name` (String) Name of the state volume, `buildx_buildkit_<node>_state`, mounted on `/var/lib/buildkit`.

<a id="nestedblock--docker_container"></a>
### Nested Schema for `docker_container`

Optional:

- `cgroup_parent` (String) Parent cgroup of the container (`cgroup-parent=`).
- `cpu_period` (Number) CPU CFS period in microseconds (`cpu-period=`).
- `cpu_quota` (Number) CPU CFS quota in microseconds per `cpu_period` (`cpu-quota=`).
- `cpu_shares` (Number) Relative CPU weight (`cpu-shares=`).
- `cpuset_cpus` (String) CPUs the container may use, e.g. `0-3` (`cpuset-cpus=`).
- `cpuset_mems` (String) NUMA memory nodes the container may use, e.g. `0` (`cpuset-mems=`).
- `default_load` (Boolean) Whether builds that ask for no output load their result into the daemon's image store (`default-load=`). Stored as a label on the node container and honoured by the provider's builds on this builder.
- `env` (Map of String) Environment variables for buildkitd (`env.<KEY>=`), e.g. proxy settings.
- `image` (String) BuildKit image (`image=`). Default `moby/buildkit:buildx-stable-1`. Pulled with `registry_auth` when missing.
- `memory` (Number) Memory limit in bytes (`memory=`).
- `memory_swap` (Number) Memory plus swap limit in bytes (`memory-swap=`); `-1` is unlimited swap.
- `network` (String) Network mode or network name for the container (`network=`), e.g. `host`. Default: the daemon's bridge.
- `restart_policy` (String) Restart policy (`restart-policy=`): `no`, `always`, `unless-stopped` (default, like buildx) or `on-failure`.


<a id="nestedblock--remote"></a>
### Nested Schema for `remote`

Optional:

- `cacert` (String) Path of the CA certificate that signed the BuildKit server certificate (`cacert=`).
- `cert` (String) Path of the client certificate presented to BuildKit (`cert=`); needs `key`.
- `key` (String) Path of the client certificate's private key (`key=`); needs `cert`.
- `servername` (String) Server name the BuildKit certificate is checked against (`servername=`). Default: the endpoint's host.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by builder name (its node container buildx_buildkit_<name>0), node name, or container ID.
terraform import docker_buildx_builder.ci ci
```

## Known issues

### `driver = "cloud"` is not verified against the live Docker Build Cloud service

Known issue `buildx-builder-cloud-unverified` (`reference/_gen/deferred.json`, kind `known_issue`). Docker Build Cloud builders are tested only against a fake auth server and a fake BuildKit proxy. Three behaviours follow buildx v0.38.2 by assumption: the provider dials the builder group at the default proxy `build-cloud.docker.com:443` (buildx looks up per-platform instances through the Hub API), it sends `buildx-version: v0.38.2`, and it loads build results through the build session (buildx's "cloud pull" is not implemented). Other drivers are not affected. To verify an account, run the live acceptance test (needs a Build Cloud subscription):

```terraform
provider "docker" {
  registry_auth {
    address  = "docker.io"
    username = var.hub_user
    password = var.hub_pat
  }
}

resource "docker_buildx_builder" "cloud" {
  name     = "cloud-builder"
  driver   = "cloud"
  endpoint = "<org>/<builder>"
}
```

```shell
TF_ACC=1 TF_ACC_BUILD_CLOUD=1 TF_ACC_BUILD_CLOUD_BUILDER=<org>/<builder> DOCKER_REGISTRY_USER=<hub user> DOCKER_REGISTRY_PASS=<hub PAT> go test -run TestAccBuildxBuilderCloud_live ./internal/provider -count=1
```
